messages:
deploybot: Starting deployment: migration=user_event_fk_change target=prod deployer=@maria window=2026-03-22T02:00Z-03:00Z. Planned lock: table user_events row-level write locks, per-shard quiesce ~30s. Backfill will run as streaming job with parallel=8. Runbook: https://go/internal/runbooks/migrations/user_event_fk_change. Will post preflight results shortly.

maria (release-lead): Quick heads-up: we've pinned services to image `redwood/service:v2.14.3` for this window to avoid schema mismatch. All write paths should respect the compatibility flag. @db-admin can you confirm index/constraint order?

db-admin: Confirmed. Plan: add fk constraint in NOT VALID state, run streaming backfill to populate missing references, then `ALTER TABLE VALIDATE CONSTRAINT` for each shard. We'll take a brief exclusive lock (~20-45s) per shard to switch references. Backfill job supports resume if interrupted.

sahil: Noted. Past runs showed row-level lock spikes when batch size too big. Recommend adding `SET lock_timeout = '5s'` in the migration session and use batch_size=500 -> try 300 if we see contention.

taylor (eng-sre): +1 on lock_timeout. I'll add a temporary Datadog metric for lock_wait > 5s on user_events and create an alert (sev3) for any sustained lock waits. Also scheduling a tiny capacity buffer on write-queue redis during the window.

maria (release-lead): Rollback plan: if we see cascading errors or p95 latency > 500ms for more than 5m, we revert the service pin to `v2.14.2` and cancel backfill jobs. @jen you'll lead the rollback call. db-admin has a rollback script to drop the pending constraint and cancel jobs.

jen (oncall): Copy. I'll be on the call +1 from window start. No external customer notice required; downtime per shard should be <1m. I'll draft a short internal post once window completes.

deploybot: Preflight checks: replicas=healthy, pg_lag=28ms, avg_cpu<60%. Starting canary on shard=0 (canary duration=3m). Reply :thumbsup: to promote.

anya (infra): Pinned kube image `redwood/service:v2.14.3` deployed to canary nodes. If we need to roll back quickly I can tag nodes back to `v2.14.2` and drain/pull within 90s.

maria (release-lead): Promoting canary. Proceed to shard rollout after 3m smoke. Keep an eye on lock_wait and p99 latency.

deploybot: Canary OK. Proceeding to full rollout. Starting backfill job `backfill_user_fk_20260322` (parallel=8).

```
backfill_user_fk_20260322: shard=0 rows_processed=120k rows_err=0 rows_remaining=880k throughput=5.2k/s
backfill_user_fk_20260322: shard=1 rows_processed=95k rows_remaining=905k throughput=4.1k/s
```

db-admin: Backfill progress: overall 12% after 4m, avg rows/s ~8k. Projected finish ~40m at current parallelism. Throttling enabled to preserve p99.

sahil: Observed a 30s lock wait spike on shard=5, backfill paused for that shard and reverted the swap. I'm going to reduce batch size to 200 for shard=5 and retry.

maria (release-lead): We're pausing rollforward for shard=5 and shard=6. Decision: continue applying to remaining shards, skip 5 & 6 and schedule a follow-up morning window to reattempt with adjusted batch size. Not doing a global rollback. @db-admin confirm safe to leave constraint NOT VALID globally.

db-admin: Confirmed. Constraint remains NOT VALID; shards 0-4,7-... applied. No FK validation run yet on skipped shards, and no data inconsistency observed. This is safe: application code still handles missing references. We'll create a remediation job for the two skipped shards next window.

taylor (eng-sre): I'll keep alerts open for 30m and watch p99. I've also increased write-queue concurrency by 10% to smooth spikes.

jen (oncall): Marking this window as completed-for-applied-shards. Follow-up action items: adjust default batch size from 500 -> 300, add preflight check for lock_wait distribution, and add a short release note line. I'll file the postmortem with these action items.

maria (release-lead): Thanks team. Good catch on shard 5/6. We'll schedule a targeted window for the remaining shards and test the lower batch size in staging first. Closing thread for this window. :white_check_mark:
